Consider the following properties of an undirected simple graph $\text{G}$ with $n$ vertices.

  1. $\text{G}$ is connected.
  2. $\text{G}$ is acyclic.
  3. $\text{G}$ has $n-1$ edges.
  4. Every two different vertices in $\text{G}$ are connected by a unique path.

Which of the following is correct?

  1. if $\text{G}$ satisfies properties (a) and (b), then $\text{G}$ satisfies property (c)
  2. if $\text{G}$ satisfies properties (a) and (c), then $\text{G}$ satisfies property (b)
  3. if $\text{G}$ satisfies properties (b) and (c), then $\text{G}$ satisfies property (a)
  4. if $\text{G}$ satisfies properties (d), then $\text{G}$ satisfies property (a), (b), (c)

A simple graph is an undirected graph in which each edge connects two different vertices and no two edges connect the same pair of vertices.
An “oriented simple graph” is a simple graph which has been converted to a digraph by assigning an orientation to each edge. The orientation of $\{u, v\}$ can be thought of as a mapping of it to either $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ but not to both.
Note that if $u$ and $v$ are different vertices then the orientation of $\{u, v\}$ is a mapping of it to either $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ but not to both. So, the following digraph is Not a oriented simple graph $:\text{V} = \{u, v\}$ and $\text{E} = \{(u, v),(v, u) \}$

What is the number of oriented simple graphs on $5$ vertices?

Let $\text{T}$ denote a nonempty binary tree in which every node either is a leaf or has two children. Then $n(\text{T})$ denotes the number of non-leaf nodes of $\text{T}$ (where $n(\text{T}) =0,$ if $\text{T}$ is a leaf), $h(\text{T})$ denotes the height of $\text{T}$ (where $h(\text{T}) =0,$ if $\text{T}$ is a leaf), $\text{T}_{\text{L}}$ denotes the left subtree of $\text{T},$ and $\text{T}_{\text{R}}$ denotes the right subtree of $\text{T}.$ If $\text{F}$ is a function defined by

$\text{F(T)}=\left\{\begin{array}{l}0\;\; \text {if T is a leaf } \\ \text{F}\left(\text{T}_{\text{L}}\right)+\text{F}\left(\text{T}_{\text{R}}\right)+\min \left(h\left(\text{T}_{\text{L}}\right), h\left(\text{T}_{\text{R}}\right)\right) \text { otherwise, }\end{array}\right.$

Then $\text{F(T)} =$

  1. $n(\text{T}) + h(\text{T}) - 1$
  2. $n(\text{T}) + h(\text{T})$
  3. $n(\text{T}) - h(\text{T}) -1$
  4. $n(\text{T}) - h(\text{T})$

  4. The size of the maximum independent set in $\text{G}$ is same as the size of maximum clique on $\text{G}.$
